questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Curves ahead.
Divided highway starts.
Divided highway ends.
Bumps in the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided highway ends.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the divided highway is ending ahead.

questions.question: When you see a steady yellow traffic light, you should:

options.text: Speed up to avoid a red light.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
Look at what the cars next to you are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a red light is coming next. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: Before you start the car, you should:

options.text: Buckle your safety belt.
Make sure all passengers have buckled their safety belts.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Make it a habit to buckle your safety belt and check that all passengers are buckled before starting the car.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Highway changes ahead and to the right.
Hiking trails ahead and to the right.
Hotel ahead and to the right.
Hospital ahead and to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hospital ahead and to the right.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that a hospital with emergency services is to the right.

questions.question: On long trips, you can avoid getting drowsy by:

options.text: Turning on your car radio.
Slowing down.
Stopping regularly to rest.
Moving your eyes from side to side while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stopping regularly to rest.
questions.explanation: Take regular breaks on long trips. Stop to rest and stretch your body, even if you do not feel tired yet.

questions.question: You have a green light at an intersection, but pedestrians are crossing against the red. You should:

options.text: Honk your horn.
Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrians.
Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.
Drive close to the pedestrians to scare them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.
questions.explanation: Always yield to pedestrians, even when you have a green light. Pedestrian safety comes first in any situation.

questions.question: When you want to pass another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Wait for a signal from the other driver.
Change lanes quickly so the other driver sees you.
Signal and pass only when it is safe.
Stay close behind the vehicle to pass faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal and pass only when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors and signal before changing lanes. Look over your left shoulder to make sure no vehicle is in your blind spot before you pass.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Keep right.
Keep left.
Pass with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep right.
questions.explanation: This yellow sign with black markings shows that a divided highway is starting. Stay in the right lane.

questions.question: You should drive at the maximum posted speed limit only:

options.text: At night.
During the day.
When conditions are ideal.

questions.correctAnswerText: When conditions are ideal.
questions.explanation: The posted speed limit is the fastest you can legally go only when conditions are perfect. Drive at a safe speed that matches the traffic around you, up to the speed limit. All drivers must drive safely at all times.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not pass.
Do not enter.
No turn on red.
Keep right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep right.
questions.explanation: This sign means a divided highway is coming. The road will split into two one-way roads with a barrier between them. Stay in the right lane.

questions.question: When must you stop at a railroad crossing?

options.text: When a flagger tells you to stop.
When there is a stop sign.
When flashing red signals and gates are working.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger tells you to stop, when there is a stop sign, or when flashing red signals and gates are working.

questions.question: At a crosswalk, what must you do?

options.text: You must yield to pedestrians.
Pedestrians must yield to you.
Construction workers must yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield to pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians have the right to cross at crosswalks. You must stop for pedestrians in a marked or unmarked crosswalk, even if there is no traffic signal.

questions.question: Which statement about bad weather driving is true?

options.text: Sudden weather changes mean you should change how you drive.
You should slow down when driving in rain or fog.
Watch for vehicles behind you during bad weather.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When weather changes suddenly, adjust your driving. Slow down in rain and fog. Be aware of vehicles behind you that may be going too fast for the conditions.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts to cross in front of you. What should you do?

options.text: Flash your lights.
Slow down.
Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian cross.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be ready to stop when you see pedestrians. Always yield to pedestrians crossing in a crosswalk. Be extra careful around children.

questions.question: What does alcohol affect?

options.text: How fast you recover from headlight glare.
Your reaction time.
Your judgment of distances.
All of these.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of these.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time, reduces your vision, changes your judgment of speed and distance, and makes you more likely to take risks. Alcohol is especially dangerous at night because it reduces your ability to see clearly from headlights.

questions.question: If you drink alcohol socially, how can you drive safely?

options.text: Drink coffee before driving.
Get a ride home from a friend who has not been drinking.
Take a cold shower before driving.
Stop drinking 30 minutes before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get a ride home from a friend who has not been drinking.
questions.explanation: The best way to stay safe is to get a ride from a friend who has not been drinking. Coffee and cold showers do not lower your blood alcohol. The body needs about one hour to eliminate one drink.

questions.question: There is no crosswalk and a pedestrian is crossing your lane. What should you do?

options.text: Make eye contact and then pass the pedestrian.
Slow down as you pass the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.
questions.explanation: Yield to pedestrians at any crosswalk, marked or unmarked. Stop and let pedestrians cross, even if there is no crosswalk.

questions.question: What are blind spots?

options.text: Spots in your vision when you are tired.
Areas of the road you cannot see in your mirrors.
Traffic control devices.

questions.correctAnswerText: Areas of the road you cannot see in your mirrors.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, look over your shoulder to check for vehicles in your blind spots. Blind spots are areas near the rear corners of your vehicle that your mirrors cannot see.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Oncoming traffic and pedestrians should yield to you.
Never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to oncoming traffic going straight. Always yield to pedestrians.

questions.question: The traffic light turns yellow as you approach an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to beat the red light.
Brake hard to stop.
Be ready to stop in the center of the intersection.
Be ready to stop before the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop before the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the red light is coming. Be ready to stop before you enter the intersection.
